'''Takeogumi-no-Mikoto''' (''takeogumi no mikoto''; dates of birth and death unknown) was a {{ill|gōzoku|ja|豪族}} of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} and the first '''{{ill|Hi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|火国造}}'''. At {{ill|Kengun Shrine|ja|健軍神社}} he is written as '''Takeogumi-no-Mikoto''' ({{lang|ja|健緒組命}}); in the ''{{ill|Hizen no Kuni Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記}}'' he appears as '''Takeogumi''' ({{lang|ja|健緒組}}) and as '''Hi-no-Kimi Takeogumi''' ({{lang|ja|火君健緒組}}; also rendered {{lang|ja|火君健緒純}}).

== Overview ==
According to the ''{{ill|Hizen no Kuni Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記}}'', during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇|lt=Emperor Sujin|lt_ja=崇神朝}}, two {{ill|tsuchigumo|ja|土蜘蛛}} chiefs named Uchizaru and Kubizaru lived on Asakuna Peak in {{ill|Mashiki District|ja|益城郡}}, leading more than 180 followers and hiding atop the mountain in refusal to submit to the emperor. The emperor commanded Takeogumi — ancestor of the Hi-no-Kimi (Hi-no-Kimi) — to subjugate the tsuchigumo. Takeogumi obeyed the imperial order and destroyed them all; while surveying the land afterward, night fell and he stopped at {{lang|ja|白髪山}} (Mt. Shiraga) in {{ill|Yatsushiro District|ja|八代郡}}.

That night a fire appeared in the empty sky, kindled of itself, gradually descended, and lit the mountain. Astonished, Takeogumi found it strange, and when he returned to court to report the suppression of the rebels he related the event. The emperor proclaimed, "I have never heard of anything like what you report. The land where fire came down should be called the '''{{ill|Land of Hi|ja|火国|lt=Hi no Kuni}}'''." He then granted Takeogumi a clan name in recognition of his deeds, calling him '''Hi-no-Kimi Takeogumi'''. Takeogumi was given the country to rule, and thus — because of the fire — it was called the Land of Hi.
